commitResults.messageBody:
Summarize the required SE-EDU Git and Java coding standards in project-local reference documents.

These references give future code changes a consistent style baseline.

Currently, Alfred does not save tasks between sessions.

This should change as users lose their task list whenever the program exits.

Saves task-list changes immediately and load saved tasks at startup.

Uses a relative, OS-independent data path so the application works on
any computer and creates its data directory only when needed.

The saved format preserves task types, statuses, descriptions, and
deadline or event details.

UI cases share a working directory, which allows saved task data to affect later cases.

This makes the test results dependent on their execution order.

Run every case in its own temporary directory and support a setup session
followed by a fresh restart-verification session.

This isolates cases while testing that saved task state is loaded correctly
after Alfred restarts.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add instruction within AGENTS.md to follow coding conventions
Add date-time support for deadline and event tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Store task dates as LocalDateTime so deadlines and events can be
validated, displayed consistently, and restored after a restart.

Accept yyyy-MM-dd and d/M/yyyy HHmm inputs, and add UI coverage
for valid formatting and invalid-date state preservation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Updated the ASCII art to include the batman logo as well
commitResults.messageBody: Currently, the ASCII art only included the word 'Alfred' and this might have been confusing to understand the context

Alfred mixed command processing with all console input and output,
which made its main method responsible for unrelated concerns.

Move the banner, command reading, task responses, separators, and
error display into Ui. This gives later Parser and TaskList extractions
a smaller coordinator to work with while preserving all user-visible
behavior.

Alfred directly owned the mutable task ArrayList, so collection
operations were spread across the application coordinator, user
interface, and storage boundary.

Introduce TaskList to encapsulate ordered task access and mutation.
Update Alfred, Ui, and Storage to depend on this domain abstraction,
while retaining the existing task order and persistent format.

Alfred contained command recognition, task-number validation, and
task-construction rules alongside application coordination.

Move those input-interpretation responsibilities into Parser. Alfred
now receives parsed command details and focuses on task updates,
storage, and user-interface coordination without altering responses.

The existing Command enum represented only recognized keywords, but the
stretch-goal design needs Command to represent executable behavior.

Rename the enum to CommandType so it continues to model input labels.
This prepares a separate Command abstraction for later increments
without changing any parsing or user-visible behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add executable list and exit commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Alfred still handled the list and exit command behaviors directly,
which prevented the command hierarchy from owning even its simplest
actions.

Introduce the Command abstraction and extract ListCommand and
ExitCommand. Parser creates these argument-free commands, while the
existing dispatcher continues to handle commands that need arguments.

Alfred still performed task-status changes and persistence directly,
duplicating the command execution pattern used by the new framework.

Add MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand, with Parser validating their task
numbers before creating them. This moves both status-update behaviors
into executable commands while retaining their existing responses.

Alfred still removed tasks, saved the updated list, and displayed the
removal response directly.

Add DeleteCommand and let Parser validate its task number before
creating it. This moves the final indexed task mutation into the
command hierarchy while preserving deletion behavior and messages.

Alfred still added parsed tasks, saved them, and displayed confirmation
directly after the other commands had moved into the command hierarchy.

Add a generic AddCommand and have Parser create it for to-do, deadline,
and event input. Alfred now consistently parses and executes a Command
for every supported user instruction.

Alfred's static main method still created every collaborator and contained
the application loop, even after commands became executable objects.

Give Alfred instance fields and a run method that loads tasks and
executes one parsed command per loop iteration. Use finally for the
response separator so exit output remains unchanged.

All application classes are in the default package, which obscures
their responsibilities and prevents a clearer project structure.

Organize application classes by responsibility under the alfred
base package.

Update the UI test runner to compile recursive source paths and
launch the packaged application entry point.

commitResults.messageTitle: Edited build.gradle to run UI tests through Gradle
commitResults.messageBody: Added the uiTest task and made Gradle's test task run the existing console UI test plan

commitResults.messageTitle: Add parser and storage JUnit tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Cover core command parsing and task persistence behavior, including
invalid input and malformed saved data.

Allow Storage to use an injected file path so tests run in isolated
temporary directories. Fix malformed deadline and event commands so
they return validation errors instead of throwing index exceptions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Package Alfred as executable fat JAR
commitResults.messageBody:
Configure the Shadow plugin output as alfred.jar and document how
to build, locate, distribute, and run the executable JAR.

Users cannot locate tasks by a keyword when their list grows. Add the
find command to match task descriptions case-insensitively and display
matching tasks in list order.

Reject missing search keywords to preserve clear command feedback. Include
JUnit and console UI coverage for matching, no-match, and invalid inputs.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap project text and refine Gradle ignores
commitResults.messageBody:
Project source, documentation, scripts, and test-plan text contain lines
over the 110-character limit. The ignore rules also exclude build.gradle,
which is version-controlled build configuration.

Wrap maintained content at 110 characters or fewer, using language-specific
continuations where needed. Keep Gradle caches and build output ignored, but
track build.gradle so build configuration changes are captured in Git.

Use formatting-only changes to preserve behavior while making the project
consistent with the configured editor limit.
